label: Hazard chain, modelled: the ensemble's median member (volume ×1, source Cv 0.2) routed down Ronti Gad → Rishiganga → Dhauliganga

run.note: 9 members (629 ms), median member re-run to the end of its recession; the mass reaches the river 1.3 min after the collapse at 67 m/s (Voellmy block, μ 0.12, ξ 2500 m/s², Zhang et al. 2022, RAMMS back-analysis of this event); it runs on down the valley as a debris flow and hands over to the routed flood at 3.4 km, 2.7 min after the collapse, at 28 m/s (no faster than the flood there); direct flow: 4.9 Mm³ of melt water, 6.2 Mm³ at Cv 0.20, peak 13921 m³/s as a debris-flow surge (peak 12 s after its front, over by 15 min)

stations.name: Ronti Gad (avalanche runout, head of the mapped stream)

observed.note: 04:51 UTC (10:21 IST): ~26.9 Mm³ of rock and ice (~80/20 %) detached from the north face of Ronti Peak at ~5,500 m — a slab up to ~550 m wide and ~80 m thick; ~8 Mm³ was deposited near the Ronti Gad–Rishiganga confluence.
RECONSTRUCTED mean discharge 8,200–14,200 m³/s at the Rishiganga plant (centre of the band shown), passing in 10–20 min; front ~25 m/s here, ~15 km from the source. The 13.2 MW plant was destroyed.
Seismic timeline: release 04:51:10 UTC, debris at the Ronti Gad–Rishiganga confluence 04:54 ("~55 m/s from the source"), Rishiganga HEP damaged 04:57 (~27 m/s, "verified with available videos").
Seismic timeline: first wave at the Tapovan HEP 05:07 UTC (~13 m/s from Raini), a second, damaging wave at 05:12 (21 min).

Seismic records put the debris flow at the Tapovan project ~15 min after the failure (Shugar et al.: ~16 m/s just upstream of Tapovan). Most of those lost that morning were workers at the two hydropower projects, many of them in the Tapovan tunnels (casualty figures are kept off screen, as in every preset).
observed.source: Cook et al. 2021, Science 374:87–92 (via The Landslide Blog); Shugar et al. 2021

observed.note: RECONSTRUCTED mean discharge 2,900–4,900 m³/s below Tapovan (centre of the band shown); front ~12 m/s.

Seismic detection of the flood at the road bridge near Joshimath at 10:58:33 IST, 34.6 km downstream, where the water rose 16 m (the earlier "~27 min from 10 m/s" was a derived figure, not a timed arrival).
observed.source: Cook et al. 2021, Science 374:87–92, doi:10.1126/science.abj1227, via the GFZ press release (secondary source)
